tool.name: GeneralRasterClassification

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/topographic-analysis/general-raster-classification.html
Classifies any single raster into categories using a saved 'general' classification system -- threshold rules on the raster's raw or whole-raster standardized (z-score) values. Similar in purpose to Esri's standard Reclassify tool, except that the classification scheme is authored once, as a reusable named system, in the Classification System Builder; that each output class stores a name (and color) with the raster; that no Spatial Analyst or 3D Analyst extension is required; and that classes can be set in standard deviations from the raster's mean as well as in its own values. The same reusable classification systems and per-user store as the Slope Position and Landform tools, but for an arbitrary raster rather than a DEM.

tool.usage:
This is the general-purpose sibling of the Slope Position and Landform tools: it applies a saved classification system to any single-band raster (elevation, an index, a model output -- anything), turning continuous values into named, colored classes. It is the direct descendant of the "General Grid Classification" function in Jeff Jenness's ArcView 3.x TPI extension (renamed here: "grid" was the raster format of the ArcView/ArcInfo era).
If you know Esri's Reclassify tool: this tool serves a similar function -- turning a continuous raster into integer classes -- so much of what you expect from Reclassify applies here. The real differences are: (1) the classification scheme is not typed into the tool dialog each time, but created once, as a reusable named system, in the standalone Classification System Builder, and then simply picked from a dropdown here; (2) each output class stores a name (label) -- and a display color -- with the raster's attribute table, so the result draws and reads as named, colored categories rather than bare integers; and (3) no additional extension is required -- Esri's Reclassify needs a Spatial Analyst or 3D Analyst license, while this tool runs on any ArcGIS Pro license; and (4) classes can be defined in standardized units as well as in the raster's own values -- thresholds in standard deviations from the mean of the whole raster, so that "more than one standard deviation above average" can be a class without first working out what value that is, whereas Reclassify works only in the raster's own values.
Each class is defined by one or two threshold conditions on the input raster, interpreted either as raw values (the raster's own units) or standardized values (a whole-raster z-score, (value minus mean) divided by standard deviation). Raw thresholds are absolute; standardized thresholds adapt to the raster's own distribution -- useful when you do not know the value range in advance, or when comparing rasters with different ranges. A cell takes a class when all of that class's conditions hold; where classes overlap, the lowest class value wins. Classification is a single vectorized pass in numpy, with no Esri Con or Spatial Analyst.
Classification systems are reusable, named JSON rule sets (thresholds, names, colors) saved in a per-user location that survives add-in reinstalls. This tool lists the 'general' systems it finds there; the bundled defaults are a basic 4-class and 7-class template using standardized bands, meant as starting points to edit in the Classification System Builder, and a forestry system, Ground-Based Equipment Operability (Percent Slope), that classifies a PERCENT-slope raster into six raw bands at 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 percent from published Forest Service and state equipment limits (a degree-slope raster needs its own system). Per-class colors symbolize the output when it is added to the map. This tool supports systems that classify a single input raster.

dialogReference.para: Any single-band raster to classify. Its values are read as-is (for raw thresholds) or standardized whole-raster (for standardized thresholds), per the chosen Classification system.

The output integer class raster, carrying a Value / Class_Name attribute table and a color map from the classification system (including any per-class opacity, so e.g. a hillshade can show through selected classes). Cells matching no class (or outside the data) are unclassified. A name is suggested from the input.

The saved general classification system to apply (thresholds, names, colors) -- this plays the role of the remap table you would type into Esri's Reclassify tool, except it is created once in the Classification System Builder and reused, and it carries a name and color for each class. The list is read from the per-user store; the bundled defaults are basic 4-class and 7-class standardized-band templates and the Ground-Based Equipment Operability (Percent Slope) forestry system.

scriptExample.title: General Raster Classification example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Classify a raster into four standardized bands. The comment block lists the bundled classification systems; pass the name exactly as shown. Any 'general' system you have created or edited in the Classification System Builder is equally valid (pass its name as shown in the Builder) -- the bundled list is not exhaustive.
scriptExample.code:
import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your installed path is shown in this tool's run messages
# ---- valid options for the list-driven parameter ------------------------- # system (bundled; user-created systems from the Classification System # Builder are also valid -- this list is not exhaustive): # "Basic 4-Class (Standardized Bands)" # "Basic 7-Class (Standardized Bands)" # "Ground-Based Equipment Operability (Percent Slope)"
arcpy.jenness.GeneralRasterClassification( in_raster="index.tif", out_raster="index_Classified.tif", system="Basic 4-Class (Standardized Bands)")

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Classify any single raster into categories using a saved classification system (raw or standardized threshold rules); no Spatial Analyst.
dataIdInfo.idAbs: Applies a saved 'general' classification system -- threshold rules (raw or whole-raster standardized values), class names, and colors -- to any single-band raster, producing an integer class raster with a Value/Class_Name attribute table and color map. Each class is an AND of one or two threshold conditions; the lowest class value wins on overlap. Classification is a single vectorized numpy pass with no Esri Con or Spatial Analyst. The reusable classification systems live in a per-user store that survives add-in reinstalls and are authored in the Classification System Builder; bundled defaults are basic 4- and 7-class standardized-band templates and the Ground-Based Equipment Operability (Percent Slope) forestry system. Descends from the General Grid Classification function of Jenness's ArcView 3.x TPI extension.
